bull.t: High product gross margins and revenue scale
bull.b: Sustained ~84% gross margins across marketed rare‑disease therapies indicate attractive unit economics that can support profitability as fixed SG&A and R&D are trimmed. High product margins provide durable cash generation potential per incremental sale once operating leverage is achieved.

bull.t: Commercial scale and durable patient reach
bull.b: Established distribution across 35+ countries and sizable reimbursed patient cohorts (Crysvita, Dojolvi, Evkeeza) reduce single‑market exposure and underpin recurring specialty sales. Durable payer relationships and geographic diversification support steadier revenue growth over multiple quarters.

Two near‑term PDUFAs represent structural inflection points: approvals would add high‑value, durable revenue streams and extend the commercial portfolio. Successful launches can markedly improve cash flow and reduce funding reliance, changing the company's multi‑year profitability profile.

bear.t: High cash burn and negative operating cash flow
bear.b: Persistently negative operating and free cash flows signal ongoing funding needs and constrain long‑term flexibility. Even with improving FCF trends, sustained cash consumption forces dependence on financings or asset sales and elevates execution risk for launches and late‑stage studies.

bear.t: Weakened balance sheet and elevated leverage
bear.b: Negative equity combined with ~ $1.2B debt materially reduces financial headroom and borrowing capacity. Elevated leverage increases refinancing and covenant risk, raises cost of capital, and makes the company more sensitive to missed milestones or delayed cash inflows.

bear.t: Profitability path reliant on PRVs and execution
bear.b: Management's path to profit assumes PRV monetization and successful launches; delays, lower PRV proceeds, or launch setbacks would materially widen funding gaps. Reliance on one‑time monetizations and timing‑sensitive events leaves long‑term outcomes contingent on external execution.
